summary: Tested the Audit Trails module (audit_trails) end to end. Backend: 18 of 18 pytest tests pass (tests/test_iter364_audit_trails.py). Verified: (1) CREATE when a PRE quote is created via POST /api/quotes with cli_sin_rif: registro_id=PRE-..., valores_anteriores=null, full snapshot, user, IP, UA and endpoint captured. (2) assign-client PRE→COT creates an UPDATE with client_id and quote_number (old/new values correct, no updated_at). (3) DELETE quote stores the full snapshot, with valores_nuevos=null and campos=null. (4) PUT security-policy gives campos_modificados exactly ['lockout_minutes']; repeating the same PUT creates NO trail. (5) Bank integration: the $push is audited as integrations[<id>]; PUT notes gives campos exactly ['integrations[<id>].notes']; a no-op PUT creates no trail; the DELETE integration is audited. (6) Client CREATE/UPDATE(fantasy_name)/DELETE are all logged. (7) Projects: PUT /api/projects/{id}/priority adds no trails. A unit check also confirmed the AuditedCollection skips writes for /api/projects* and /api/direct-projects* even on audited collections such as quotes. (8) Filters: combined filters, pagination, field and registro work; total and total_all are consistent; detail returns 404 for a bad id; a bad date returns 400; unauthenticated calls are rejected; PUT/DELETE/PATCH/POST on trails return 404/405; export returns a valid xlsx with only the filtered module. (9) RBAC: a non-admin TEST user gets 403 on list, filters and export, 200 after special_permissions=['configuracion:auditor'], and 403 again after revert. (10) Login of a user that already has menu_groups creates no trail; change-password creates an UPDATE with password_hash shown as '***'. UI: the Settings tile (inside the collapsed 'Configuración General' accordion) and the Security button both navigate to /settings/audit-trails. The page shows the counter, filters (modules multi-select, action select, field, reset), a table with no edit or delete buttons, and a detail dialog with the diff in red/green plus IP, UA and endpoint metadata. Excel export downloads. A non-admin auditor user sees the tile and the page, the back link goes to 'Configuración', and the Security tile is hidden. There were no backend 500s during the run.

minor.issue: The regex (password|passwd|hash|token|secret|otp|api_key|apikey) is substring-based, so it over-masks business fields. Verified: include_tokenizador, tokenizador_items, otp_ttl_minutes, otp_enabled, password_max_age_days, password_history_count, min_password_length, pdf_hash and hashtags are all stored as '***'. As a result, an auditor cannot see old/new values for most Security Policy changes (password age, length, OTP/2FA settings) or for the quote Tokenizador flags. Fix: match exact key names or word boundaries (e.g. ^(password|password_hash|.*_token|token|secret|otp_code|otp_hash|api_key)$) and keep config fields readable.

Writes made by unauthenticated flows are attributed to 'Anónimo' instead of the user involved. Examples: the menu_groups auto-migration in _issue_session (seen live), locked_until on lockout, and the forced password change. Suggest calling set_audit_user(user) in these handlers once the user is identified.
openpyxl builds up to 50k rows synchronously inside an async handler, which blocks the event loop. Consider run_in_threadpool.

Every update/delete now runs 1–2 extra reads (find before, find after). update_many/delete_many log at most 500 docs, so larger bulk operations are only partly audited. bulk_write, aggregate($merge/$out) and with_options() fall through __getattr__ and are not audited. None of these are used today, but this should be documented.

A long-lived task started with asyncio.create_task from inside a request (rather than at startup) inherits that request's context. Its later writes would then be attributed to that user and endpoint instead of 'Sistema'. Worth checking for lazily started schedulers.

issues: The 'Pistas de Auditoría' tile is hidden inside the collapsed 'Configuración General' accordion, so it is hard to find. It is visible after clicking general-config-toggle.
Registro ID for Bancos shows the bank name (e.g. '100% Banco') rather than an ID. It is readable, but searching by bank_id only works through entidad_id.
The /settings/audit-trails route is not role-guarded on the frontend. A non-auditor who opens it directly gets an error toast and an empty page, not a redirect. The backend correctly returns 403.

action_items: Narrow SENSITIVE_RE so that non-secret fields (otp_ttl_minutes, otp_enabled, password_max_age_days, min_password_length, password_history_count, include_tokenizador, pdf_hash) are not masked. Keep masking password_hash, password_history, tokens, secrets and OTP codes.
(Optional) Call set_audit_user in the login, expired-password and lockout flows so trails are not 'Anónimo'.
(Optional) Run the Excel export in a threadpool.
critical_code_review_comments: audit_trail.py: SENSITIVE_RE over-masking (see minor issue). This is the main functional gap for auditing Security Policy changes.
audit_trail.py _log: UPDATE masks twice (_mask on the dict, then again on each key); it works but is redundant.
The interceptor scope is correct: _skip on the path prefix covers all write methods; find_one_and_delete checks _skip after the delete, which is fine.
routes/audit_trails.py: when the user and registro filters are combined, the code mixes $or with $and; this works, but building the whole query under $and would be cleaner.
seed_data_creation: Test data was created and then removed. A TEST quote PRE→COT-2026-11-070-PYME was deleted through the API (its sequence number is consumed). A TEST client was deleted through the API, and a TEST bank integration on '100% Banco' was deleted through the API. Security policy lockout_minutes was reverted to its original value. TEST users test_iter364_*@example.com and test_iter364_ui@example.com were inserted and deleted directly in Mongo, without audit. The audit trails produced by the tests remain, since they are immutable.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=$(grep REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL /app/frontend/.env|cut -d= -f2) python -m pytest tests/test_iter364_audit_trails.py -p no:xdist. Banks have no integrations by default, so the test creates its own. A TEST user without menu_groups produces a menu_groups UPDATE trail on first login; the test includes menu_groups to avoid this. Profiles do not include configuracion:auditor, so the special-permissions ceiling blocks it for users that have a profile_id; RBAC tests use a TEST user without a profile. The Settings tile lives under the general-config-toggle accordion.
